items.title: Canada vs Guatemala: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Canada vs Guatemala in the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League. Canada and Guatemala meet again just days after their last meeting, with both camps naming unchanged-look lineups for the rematch in this Concacaf Nations League fixture.
Canada come into this one off a 3-2 win over this same Guatemala side on November 14, a result that showed they can get the job done even when they do not shut the door defensively. That match also marked their most recent outing, so Mauro Biello’s group will look to carry the same attacking edge into this second meeting. Another result here would keep Canada’s momentum rolling in this Nations League cycle.
Guatemala head into this match on the back of a 2-3 loss to Canada on November 14, a game in which they scored twice but still came up short. Before that, they had beaten Suriname 1-0 on October 6, showing they can grind out low-scoring wins when needed. Luis Fernando Tena’s side will be looking to flip the script against the same opponent and respond with a better result this time.
Canada confirmed lineup
Canada line up in a 4-4-2 with Maxime Crépeau behind a back line of Niko Sigur, Luc De Fougerolles, Joel Waterman and Richie Laryea. Mathieu Choinière and Nathan Saliba sit in midfield alongside wide options Tajon Buchanan and Liam Millar, giving Biello’s side width and the ability to get bodies forward quickly. Jonathan David partners Tani Oluwaseyi up front, pairing David’s finishing with Oluwaseyi’s movement. There are no absences to account for, so Canada field what looks like their strongest available group.
Canada confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Maxime Crépeau, Niko Sigur, Richie Laryea, Mathieu Choinière, Luc De Fougerolles, Joel Waterman, Tajon Buchanan, Nathan Saliba, Tani Oluwaseyi, Jonathan David, Liam Millar. Coach: Mauro Biello.
Guatemala confirmed lineup
Guatemala also set up in a 4-4-2, with Kenderson Navarro in goal protected by Aarón Herrera, Nicolás Samayoa, Allen Yanes and José Morales across the back. Rodrigo Saravia and José Rosales anchor the midfield while Óscar Santis and Jesús López provide width to support the front line. Rubio Rubín and Jehú Fajardo lead the attack, with Tena asking his front two to work off service from the flanks. With no absences listed, Guatemala are able to pick from a full squad for this rematch.
Guatemala confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Kenderson Navarro, Aarón Herrera, José Morales, Rodrigo Saravia, Allen Yanes, Nicolás Samayoa, Óscar Santis, José Rosales, Rubio Rubín, Jehú Fajardo, Jesús López. Coach: Luis Fernando Tena.

The Brazilian forward has faced increased scrutiny during a difficult start to the current campaign, but his latest comments offer insight into how he views expectations placed on modern players. 
Vinicius Junior has opened up about the pressure of maintaining elite performances at Real Madrid, reflecting on the remarkable standards set by Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi. The Brazilian forward has faced increased scrutiny during a difficult start to the current campaign, but his latest comments offer insight into how he views expectations placed on modern players.



With his performances attracting attention ahead of international duty with Brazil, Vinicius has acknowledged the challenge of remaining at the highest level throughout an entire career. The Real Madrid star also addressed the factors behind his recent struggles, while making clear that he remains determined to improve.



The Brazil international has endured a quieter opening to the 2026-27 season than many would have expected, recording one goal and three assists in 12 La Liga appearances. His output has attracted criticism as Real Madrid looks to maintain its position among the leading contenders in Spain.



Several factors have reportedly contributed to his slower start, including limited preparation time following the 2026 World Cup, transfer speculation and a four-match suspension in La Liga. Those circumstances have disrupted his rhythm, although the Brazilian remains an important part of Los Blancos’ attacking plans.



Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid (2026)



Pressure of performing at highest level



The discussion around the 26-year-old forward comes amid the enormous expectations placed on players who become the faces of major clubs and national teams. His performances are frequently compared with those of soccer’s greatest forwards, making consistency a particularly important part of the conversation.



Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi spent years producing extraordinary numbers season after season, setting a benchmark that few players have managed to approach. Vinicius recognizes the difficulty of sustaining that level, particularly in an era when players are constantly judged on their latest performances.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal shakes hands with Lionel Messi of Argentina



Vinicius explains why Ronaldo and Messi are different



Speaking ahead of Brazil’s international commitments, Vinicius addressed the comparisons and explained why maintaining such extraordinary consistency is an exceptional achievement. He singled out Ronaldo and Messi as the only players he believes managed to produce the same level of numbers over so many years.



“Staying at such a high level for so long is very difficult. I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and Messi managed to do it for so many years, consistently putting up the same numbers,” Vinicius said at a press conference.



💬 Vinicius: "Solo Cristiano Ronaldo y Messi han mantenido su nivel durante tantos años" 🗣️ "Soy humano y fallo muchas veces. En el momento más decisivo de la temporada siempre estoy ahí" pic.twitter.com/sR3xEtETJI— Mundo Deportivo (@mundodeportivo) November 16, 2026 



The Brazilian also reminded critics that he is still learning and cannot be expected to deliver perfect performances every time he steps onto the pitch. “I’m human, and I make mistakes many times, but I’m always trying to improve. Nevertheless, I am still 26 years old, and I have the right to enjoy life a little too,” he added.



His comments reflect an understanding of the demands that come with playing for Real Madrid, where expectations remain exceptionally high regardless of a player’s age or previous achievements. Vinicius is determined to improve while also recognizing the importance of finding a balance between soccer and his personal life.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo was not deceived as Jorge Jesus singles out what he promised Portugal’s legend before joining him at Al-Nassr
items.description:
The national team coach has addressed their time working together at Al-Nassr, revisiting a promise that has taken on added significance amid the recent controversy surrounding Ronaldo’s departure. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement continues to dominate the headlines in Portugal, with Jorge Jesus now offering a fresh insight into his relationship with the former captain. The national team coach has addressed their time working together at Al-Nassr, revisiting a promise that has taken on added significance amid the recent controversy surrounding Ronaldo’s departure.



Jesus’ comments come after Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, accused Portugal of failing to appreciate her son, while the national team attempts to move forward following a disappointing start to life without its all-time leading scorer. The coach has maintained that Ronaldo’s legacy remains unquestionable, despite the tensions that surrounded the final months of his international career.



Aveiro recently launched a public attack on Portugal following its 4-1 defeat to Denmark, the first match since Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5. Speaking during a ceremony at Sporting’s José Alvalade Stadium, she claimed her son had been deceived and suggested he had not received the respect he deserved.



“Of course he was sad. They deceived him. And I’m sad too,” she said, before admitting she was pleased with the Selecao’s defeat because she believed the result was deserved. She also criticized the tribute organized for Ronaldo in Braga, insisting it should have taken place in his presence rather than after his departure.



😳🇵🇹 LA MADRE DE CRISTIANO RONALDO, DURÍSIMA CONTRA PORTUGAL:“La derrota contra Dinamarca estaba BIEN MERECIDA, ESTABA CONTENTA POR ELLO. El homenaje debería haberse realizado en su presencia. Es aquí, en el Sporting, donde le vamos a rendir homenaje. Aquí se reconoce su…— Ataque Futbolero (@AtaqueFutbolero) November 16, 2026 



Ronaldo’s relationship with Jesus came under scrutiny



The controversy surrounding Ronaldo’s exit is closely connected to his relationship with Jesus, who previously coached him at Al-Nassr before taking charge of Portugal. Tensions reportedly developed over the forward’s involvement and playing time, with Ronaldo eventually leaving the national team camp during the October international window.



Jesus has defended his decisions as those of a manager acting in the team’s interests, insisting that no individual player should dictate his approach. The situation has attracted further attention following Aveiro’s accusations, but the coach has now offered a more personal account of his connection with the Portuguese superstar.



Head coach Jorge Jesus interacts with Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr



Jesus reveals what he promised Ronaldo at Al-Nassr



Speaking ahead of Portugal’s Nations League match against Wales, Jesus described Ronaldo as a lasting icon of Portuguese soccer and recalled the commitment he made when joining Al-Nassr. The coach insisted he had kept his word and had never deceived the forward about his intentions.



“Cris is a legend of Portuguese football. The Portuguese national team and Portuguese football will never be able to forget him,” Jesus said. He then explained: “As his friend, I worked with him for a year, and I got to know him personally. When I went to Al-Nassr, I told him: ‘I’m going there, and I’ll help you become champions.’ I didn’t deceive him.”



🚨 𝐉𝐎𝐑𝐆𝐄 𝐉𝐄𝐒𝐔𝐒: "𝐀𝐒 𝐇𝐈𝐒 𝐅𝐑𝐈𝐄𝐍𝐃, 𝐈 𝐖𝐎𝐑𝐊𝐄𝐃 𝐖𝐈𝐓𝐇 𝐇𝐈𝐌 𝐅𝐎𝐑 𝐀 𝐘𝐄𝐀𝐑"🇵🇹🗣 Jorge Jesus:"Cris is a legend of Portuguese football. The Portuguese national team and Portuguese football will never be able to forget him.As his friend, I worked…— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) November 16, 2026 



Jesus also acknowledged that Ronaldo’s international departure is now a reality that Portugal must accept. “The situation is a reality. We all know it and are prepared for it,” he added, making clear that the squad has to concentrate on its future rather than remain caught up in the controversy.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s absence no longer a leadership problem for Portugal as Ruben Neves reveals who will step up
items.description:
The midfielder has addressed the ongoing discussion surrounding the former captain, offering an insight into the atmosphere inside the dressing room and explaining why the squad remains confident despite the constant attention. 
Cristiano Ronaldo‘s international retirement has left Portugal facing questions about its future, but Ruben Neves believes the national team has enough experience and leadership to move forward. The midfielder has addressed the ongoing discussion surrounding the former captain, offering an insight into the atmosphere inside the dressing room and explaining why the squad remains confident despite the constant attention.



Ronaldo’s departure has continued to dominate press conferences, with Portugal’s performances regularly being compared to the period when the legendary forward was part of the team. Neves, however, insists that the situation has not disrupted the squad’s unity or affected its performances on the pitch.



The midfielder believes the continued media attention is the main reason the subject remains prominent. Speaking about when the discussion might finally disappear, Neves suggested that the focus needs to shift back towards football. “As for when this will end, I think it will end when the questions and interviews about this topic stop. Cristiano himself put an end to it by issuing an official statement,” the 29-year-old explained to reporters, via Sport TV.



He also acknowledged that the veteran’s status makes the questions understandable, but hopes the players will eventually be able to concentrate on their responsibilities without repeatedly discussing the former captain. According to Neves, the external attention has not affected the team’s atmosphere or performances.



Rúben Neves: "Foi o próprio Cristiano a colocar um ponto final e a fazer um comunicado quando terminou a sua participação na Seleção" pic.twitter.com/sJegp0AwGW— Cabine Desportiva (@CabineSport) November 16, 2026 



Portugal insists Ronaldo’s departure has not affected team harmony



Neves was particularly keen to dismiss suggestions that the constant debate has created problems within the dressing room. The Al-Hilal midfielder explained that the positive atmosphere he has experienced throughout his years with Portugal remains unchanged. “This external noise doesn’t affect us at all; it doesn’t have any impact on our performance or the atmosphere within our group,” he said. 



He added that the team spirit and harmony have remained consistent since he first joined the national setup. The midfielder also acknowledged that the squad remains grateful for everything Ronaldo contributed during his international career. However, he believes the responsibility now belongs to the players who continue representing Portugal.



Ruben Neves and Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal acknowledge the fans



“Cristiano released a statement when he ended his international career. We are forever grateful to him for everything he gave. But we understand that the responsibility now lies with us, and we must represent the national team and bear that responsibility,” Neves said.



Neves reveals who will take over Portugal’s leadership role



With Ronaldo no longer part of the squad, questions have naturally emerged about who will become the team’s main dressing-room figures. Neves believes Portugal has several experienced players capable of sharing those responsibilities rather than relying on one individual to replace the former captain.



“It’s normal; there are leaders, and luckily we have several. The more experienced players are trying to help the younger players. The atmosphere is great, and there are many players capable of taking on that role,” he explained.



Cristiano Ronaldo and Ruben Neves 



Neves also highlighted the importance of helping younger players adapt to international soccer, insisting that the transition has happened naturally. “Fortunately, our national team has many players with leadership qualities, so it’s a natural fit for us and the team as a whole,” he added.



He believes the squad has enough experience to guide the next generation, making Ronaldo’s departure less of a leadership concern than some outside observers suggest. The midfielder’s comments indicate that responsibility will be shared across the dressing room rather than transferred to a single successor.

items.title: Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come
items.description: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright“With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final. Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. And then England turned up at the Metropolitano.A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would too, but it wasn’t to be. Continue reading...

items.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managersSign up for our free newsletter hereWho should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom SAlthough the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. items.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
items.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreakLast week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result.Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. Continue reading...

items.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
items.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL drawSonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Suzanne WrackMatch report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City Continue reading...

items.title: France vs Turkey: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for France vs Turkey in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League. France and Turkey meet in the Nations League with the hosts looking to settle after a rocky November and the visitors still searching for any kind of result to build on.
France come into this one off a 1-3 loss to Italy on November 12, a result that snapped the momentum they built from a 4-1 win over Belgium on October 5 and a 1-1 draw with Italy on October 2. The dip against Italy stung, but the Belgium result showed what this group can do when the attack clicks. A win here would go a long way toward steadying the ship before the next international window.
Turkey arrive having lost all three of their last outings, falling 1-2 to Belgium on November 12 after a 1-3 defeat to Italy on October 5 and a 0-3 loss to Belgium on October 2. The pattern is clear: Turkey have struggled to find the net or keep games close against top opposition. This match is a chance to avoid a fourth straight defeat and show some sign of progress.
France confirmed lineup

The midfield trio of Eduardo Camavinga, Lucas Da Cunha and Warren Zaire-Emery gives the side balance between ball retention and running power, while Michael Olise, Kylian Mbappe and Bradley Barcola form an attacking front three with real pace and goal threat. There are no listed absences, so France should field close to a full-strength group, and the challenge will be converting their attacking talent into the kind of control that was missing against Italy.

Salih Ozcan and Orkun Kokcu sit as the double pivot, screening for a front four of Arda Guler, Yunus Akgun and Baris Alper Yilmaz behind lone striker Enes Unal. With no absences listed, this is close to the strongest group available, and the shape is built to stay compact and look to Guler and Unal for a spark going forward. Turkey will need more composure on the ball than in recent games if they hope to avoid another lopsided scoreline.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement marks new low after Portugal drops out of FIFA’s top 5 following heavy defeat as new ranking position emerges
items.description:
The setback against Denmark has also had consequences beyond the pitch, raising fresh questions about Portugal’s standing among the world’s leading sides. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement has coincided with a difficult start to a new chapter for Portugal, with Jorge Jesus facing an early test as the national team attempts to move forward without its long-time captain. The setback against Denmark has also had consequences beyond the pitch, raising fresh questions about Portugal’s standing among the world’s leading sides.



Portugal endured a disappointing evening on Saturday, suffering a 4-1 home defeat to Denmark at the Braga Municipal Stadium. The encounter marked the national team’s first appearance since Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5, bringing an end to one of the most successful careers in international soccer.



Denmark took control shortly before half-time when Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg converted a penalty in the 43rd minute. Rasmus Hojlund then struck twice in the opening stages of the second half, scoring in the 50th and 57th minutes, before Joachim Andersen added a fourth in the 75th minute.



Bernardo Silva managed to score a late consolation goal in stoppage time, but the Selecao could not prevent a heavy defeat on home soil. The result was particularly disappointing for Jesus, whose first match in this new era ended with Portugal suffering one of their most damaging recent setbacks.









Ronaldo’s departure marks beginning of new era



The defeat came just days after Ronaldo officially brought his 23-year international career to a close, having represented Portugal 234 times and scored a record 146 goals. The 41-year-old leaves behind an extraordinary legacy, having captained the national team to Euro 2016 and further international success in the UEFA Nations League.



His departure also creates a significant leadership gap for Jesus, who must now build a team capable of competing without the forward who defined Portugal’s attacking identity for more than two decades. Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs wore a redesigned No. 7 shirt against Denmark, paying tribute to the number Ronaldo made famous during his international career.



Tempo de estrear um novo 7. Porque há um que será eterno ∞🐐 pic.twitter.com/UCozRU3t89— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 14, 2026 



The transition is particularly meaningful given that Ronaldo’s son has also started making his own way through Portugal’s youth ranks. Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. recently made his Portugal U17 debut, offering a glimpse of the next generation as his father’s senior international journey comes to an end.



Portugal falls in the provisional FIFA rankings



The consequences of the defeat were immediately reflected in the provisional FIFA Men’s World Rankings, where Portugal dropped two places from fifth to seventh. The national team lost 10.09 ranking points, taking its total down to 1,797.60, with Brazil moving into sixth place.



Portugal in new FIFA rankings



The movement also allowed Morocco to return to the top five, climbing to fifth position with 1,805.34 points. The Atlas Lions had already benefited from Brazil’s 3-2 defeat to Japan before Portugal’s loss to Denmark confirmed their latest improvement.



The updated provisional top seven consists of Spain, Argentina, France, England, Morocco, Brazil and Portugal. However, these positions remain subject to FIFA’s next official update, scheduled for November 18, 2026.

items.title: Zinedine Zidane slams rumors of tension with Kylian Mbappe: ‘It’s a shame and quite annoying’
items.description:
Zinedine Zidane dismissed reports of friction with Kylian Mbappe and confirmed that the Real Madrid forward is back for France’s Nations League match against Turkey. 
Zinedine Zidane has decided to speak out about one of the topics that has surrounded France’s camp in recent days. Ahead of the Nations League match against Turkey on Sunday, the coach addressed the rumors of a complicated relationship with Kylian Mbappe and made it clear that he is not pleased with what is being said.



In the pre-match press conference, Zidane did not hide his discomfort with the reports. “I don’t understand it, but it’s not a big deal, which is why I’m not going to get into the debate. I have the relationship of a coach with his player and everything is going perfectly. I can’t stop things from being said, but they are nonsense. It’s a shame and quite annoying,” he explained.



The speculation began when several French media outlets reported that Mbappe’s relationship with Zidane was less fluid than the one he had with Didier Deschamps.



One of the possible points of friction is said to be his role on the pitch, since in Zidane’s first matches in charge the coach placed him on the left wing, with Ousmane Dembele as the center forward, a decision that reportedly caused some discomfort. However, the former Real Madrid coach moved to dismiss all the rumors, insisting that the relationship between them is very good.




🚨🇫🇷 Zinedine Zidane: “The relationship between Mbappé and me is very good”.“It really annoys me to have these fake controversies surrounding him”. pic.twitter.com/TDVcAB7Utz— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 14, 2026




Mbappe is back for the match against Turkey



Beyond the rumors, the most relevant news for France is that Mbappe will be back in the squad. Zidane confirmed that the forward is available for the match against Turkey, after he missed the 3-1 defeat to Italy as a precaution because of muscle discomfort. “It changes everything, we prefer having him than not having him. There is no problem, he will be with us tomorrow,” the coach said.


        


What is still unknown is where he will play. Asked whether he would use him on the left wing again or in the center of the attack, Zidane kept the mystery: “You will see how we play. These are coach matters”.



With the noise around his relationship with Mbappe set aside, the focus now returns to the pitch, where France has a chance to react after the first defeat of the Zidane era. 



Even if a point could be enough to secure its place in the final phase, the coach made it clear that the goal is to win, and that will be the first real test of how his team plays with its captain back.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo appears to skip Portugal’s tribute as Al Nassr shares images of him training in Saudi Arabia
items.description:
Al Nassr shared a post of Cristiano Ronaldo working with the club in Saudi Arabia, on the day Portugal prepares a tribute in Braga against Denmark. 
Portugal will pay tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo on Saturday in Braga, but the guest of honor may not be there to see it. On the day of the ceremony, Al Nassr shared images of the forward training in Saudi Arabia, which suggests that he will not travel to Portugal for the match against Denmark.



The homage is the first since Ronaldo retired from the national team on Nov. 5. All of Portugal’s players are set to walk onto the pitch wearing the No. 7 shirt, and the stadium is expected to rise for a standing ovation in the seventh minute.



Al Nassr, meanwhile, shared a post showing Ronaldo at work with the club. “The calendar pauses. The work doesn’t,” read the caption, a reference to the pause in the calendar because of the international break. The message does not mention Portugal or the tribute, but it shows that he is working with his club in Saudi Arabia while the national teams play.



His presence in Braga had not been confirmed in the days leading up to the match, and there has been no official statement that rules it out. The images from Saudi Arabia, however, point toward the most likely scenario: that Ronaldo will watch the tribute from afar, after a retirement that followed tensions with coach Jorge Jesus.




The calendar pauses. The work doesn't ⚡ pic.twitter.com/4txDgLOvA0— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) November 14, 2026




What’s next for Ronaldo with Al Nassr



Ronaldo returns to club action with Al Nassr in good form. The team is third in the Saudi Pro League with 28 points after 11 matches, two behind leaders Al Hilal, and arrives unbeaten in its last five league games, with four wins and a draw. Its next challenge comes on Friday, Nov. 20, away to Al Ahli, which sits sixth with 21 points.


        


The match also matters for the race for the Golden Boot. Ronaldo has scored eight goals in 10 appearances, which places him third among the league’s top scorers, but the leader is precisely Al Ahli’s Ivan Toney, who has 13. A strong performance against Toney’s team could help the Portuguese forward close part of that gap.



After that trip, Al Nassr faces a busy schedule, with the AFC Champions League match against Al Sadd on Nov. 24, followed by league games against Al Hazem on Nov. 28 and Al Qadsiah on Dec. 4. 



Ronaldo will have several chances to add to his tally, not only to climb the scoring chart in Saudi Arabia, but also to move closer to his personal goal of reaching 1,000 career goals, a mark that is now 15 goals away.

items.title: Portugal vs Denmark: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Portugal vs Denmark in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League. Portugal and Denmark meet again just days after their last meeting, and this time Jorge Jesus’s side gets to host the rematch.
Portugal have won their last two outings, beating Denmark 4-2 on October 1 before following up with a 2-1 win over Norway on October 4. Gonçalo Ramos and João Félix lead a dangerous front line that has found goals in bunches over those two matches. Another win here would stretch their momentum further and send a clear message in this Nations League group.
Denmark bounced back from that loss to Portugal with a 1-0 win over Wales on October 4, a result that steadied things after conceding four goals just three days earlier. Brian Riemer’s side showed defensive discipline in that narrow victory, a contrast to the openness of the first meeting with Portugal. A positive result in Lisbon would go a long way toward erasing the memory of that 4-2 defeat.
Portugal confirmed lineup
Jesus sets Portugal up in a 4-2-3-1, with Palhinha and Vitinha screening the back four and giving Bruno Fernandes freedom to link play ahead of them. Bernardo Silva and João Félix flank Fernandes in support of Gonçalo Ramos, giving the attack rotation and movement across the front line. Dalot and Nazinho provide width from fullback, while Dias and Renato Veiga anchor the center of defense. There are no absences to account for, so Jesus can call on his strongest available group.
Portugal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Diogo Costa, Alberto Costa, Diogo Dalot, Vitinha, Rúben Dias, Renato Veiga, Pedro Neto, Rúben Neves, Gonçalo Ramos, João Félix, Bruno Fernandes. Coach: Jorge Fernando Pinheiro de Jesus.
Denmark confirmed lineup
Riemer lines Denmark up in a 4-4-2, pairing Rasmus Hojlund with William Osula up front to keep a direct focus to their attack. Isaksen and Daramy work the flanks in midfield, feeding the strikers and tracking back to support Kristensen and Maehle at fullback. Hjulmand and Froholdt sit centrally to control tempo and protect a back line of Andersen and Provstgaard. With no absences reported, Riemer named his first-choice lineup for the trip to Lisbon.
Denmark confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Mads Hermansen, Alexander Bah, Joakim Mæhle, Pierre-Emile Højbjerg, Oliver Provstgaard, Joachim Andersen, Gustav Isaksen, Morten Hjulmand, Rasmus Højlund, Mikkel Damsgaard, Mohamed Daramy. Coach: Brian Riemer.

items.title: Why is Cristiano Ronaldo not playing for Portugal vs Denmark in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 5?
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo is missing from Portugal’s team sheet against Denmark for the first time in a long time, in a match that begins a new era for Jorge Jesus’s squad. 
Portugal hosts Denmark on Saturday in Braga, in the fifth round of the Nations League, with a name missing from the team sheet that has been there for more than two decades: Cristiano Ronaldo.



The explanation is that Ronaldo is no longer part of the team. On Nov. 5, the 41-year-old announced his retirement from international soccer in a video alongside a short message: “Portugal will always be in me”. He leaves as the all-time leader in appearances and goals for his country, with 146 goals in 234 caps, after a career that began in August 2003.



His departure did not come in the best way. It followed weeks of tension with coach Jorge Jesus, which began in September when the coach left him on the bench during the Nations League win over Norway.



After that match, Ronaldo left the national team camp, explaining later that he felt the coach had not kept his word, and he was suspended for 30 days. When the retirement arrived, Jesus said he had tried to change his mind. “I asked him to continue with me because I needed him by my side, but I have to accept his decision,” the Portuguese coach explained.




Caps: 234Goals: 146Legacy: ∞𝙊𝙗𝙧𝙞𝙜𝙖𝙙𝙤, 𝘾𝙖𝙥𝙞𝙩𝙖̃𝙤 pic.twitter.com/hH5Ilan87m— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 5, 2026




Who will wear Portugal’s No. 7 now?



For now, the shirt will belong to Carlos Forbs. The 22-year-old Club Brugge winger appears with the No. 7 in the official match sheet against Denmark, and he will be the first player to wear it with the new design. The Portuguese Football Federation announced that, starting today, the No. 7 will have a new design in order to immortalize the one that Ronaldo wore for 23 years.


        


The young Portugal winger has one advantage: he is not a stranger to the number, as he already wore it in the 9-1 win over Armenia in 2025. Still, the assignment is expected to be temporary.



National teams must give each player a number from 1 to 23 in this competition, so someone had to take it, and Rafael Leao, who is injured for both matches of this window, is the player most likely to inherit it later.



Portugal now has to learn how to play without the player who defined the team for more than two decades, and the match in Braga will be the first answer. Between tributes for Ronaldo and a new name on the No. 7, the squad takes its first steps in a new chapter that begins without him on the pitch.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s No. 7 immortalized for Portugal as federation unveils new design for a new era
items.description:
Portugal will mark Cristiano Ronaldo’s legacy with a redesigned No. 7, first worn by Carlos Forbs against Denmark, while the entire squad also plans a tribute in Braga. 
Portugal has found a new way to honor Cristiano Ronaldo. On Saturday, the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) announced a change in the design of the No. 7 on the national team shirt, a decision that arrives in the first match since the forward’s retirement.



In a statement, the FPF explained that the idea is to preserve what the number means for the country. “This is another way to eternalize the meaning of such a special number and honor the legacy it represents. Because there are stories, memories, achievements, and emotions that will forever be linked to Cristiano Ronaldo,” the federation said.



The new design, according to the statement, will keep the same essence but with a different look. “From today we will thus have a different number 7 on the shirt, with the same essence and the same pride, reserving the previous one for the eternalization of a story that will never be forgotten. Thank you, Cristiano!” the FPF added.



The difference is a small stroke on the numeral, which leaves the original 7 without the stroke reserved for Ronaldo. The change takes effect in the match against Denmark in Braga, in the Nations League, where Carlos Forbs will be the first player to wear the number Cristiano wore for more than 20 years.




Tempo de estrear um novo 7. Porque há um que será eterno ∞🐐 pic.twitter.com/UCozRU3t89— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 14, 2026




A second tribute is planned for Braga



The new design is not the only gesture that Portugal has prepared for Ronaldo. The entire squad is set to walk onto the pitch wearing the No. 7 shirt, an idea that the federation agreed on with coach Jorge Jesus and the team’s captains earlier this week.


        


The homage will also continue during the match, as play is expected to be stopped in the seventh minute so the stadium can give the forward a standing ovation. Away from the pitch, the federation has also left his room at the national team’s training base empty during this camp.



With both gestures, Portugal gives Ronaldo a farewell that goes beyond the pitch, in a country where his name has been tied to the national team for more than two decades. The No. 7 will keep being worn by others, but the new design makes sure that the original one, the one that carried his story, belongs only to him.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s retirement leaves its mark on Argentina: low ticket sales force closed sections vs Uruguay
items.description:
Argentina lost to Uruguay in its first match without Lionel Messi, and the national team’s friendly was played with closed sections at La Bombonera. 
Argentina’s first match since Lionel Messi’s retirement came with an unusual image off the pitch. For the friendly against Uruguay on Friday, La Bombonera, Boca Juniors’ stadium in Buenos Aires, did not have the atmosphere that is usually seen at national team games, in a night that ended with a 2-1 loss for the home side.



The reason was low demand for tickets, which led to the closure of several sections. Of the eight sections put on sale, some did not even open and the fans who had bought tickets were relocated, which made the lack of fans in the stadium evident.



The stands below the Uruguay supporters were not enabled, since the tickets for that area could not be sold, and part of the seats above the press area also remained closed.



As a result, the panoramic view of the stadium showed several gaps, something that had not been seen in Argentina matches for years. The contrast with Messi’s farewell is striking: on Oct. 6, more than 85,000 fans filled the Monumental to say goodbye to him against Benin, in a night that felt like a national celebration.



General view inside the stadium prior to the friendly between Argentina and Uruguay. (Getty Images)



The empty sections have nothing to do with the sanction that FIFA imposed on Argentina for discriminatory chants at the World Cup, which suggests that the lack of fans could be due to Messi’s absence from the pitch. 



The punishment consisted of two home matches with 50% capacity, but only the first was served, against Bolivia on Sept. 30, while the second was suspended for a one-year probation period.


        


Mac Allister reacts to the lack of fans



Alexis Mac Allister was asked about the atmosphere in the mixed zone after the match, and the Liverpool midfielder first pointed to what the team can control. “We focus on what we can handle: that this team keeps growing, that we play good soccer, and that this attracts people to keep coming to the stadium,” he said.



Then he acknowledged the effect of Messi’s absence. “It’s normal for these things to happen when Leo is no longer here, because in the end he’s the best in the world and there were people who came to see him,” he added. Even so, he put the responsibility on the squad: “But, as I said, as a team we now have to take charge and play well and win so that people feel good and want to come see us”.



Argentina’s new era is only beginning, and the first result of it was a defeat on the pitch and a half-empty stadium. The challenge for Scaloni’s team is now to turn the post-Messi curiosity into new reasons for fans to return, something that will depend as much on results as on the identity this group manages to build.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s No. 7 shirt won’t stay empty: Portugal confirm who will wear it against Denmark
items.description:
Carlos Forbs will wear the No. 7 against Denmark, a number that Luis Figo and Ronaldo made famous and that Rafael Leao is expected to inherit. 
Portugal begins a new era on Saturday, when it hosts Denmark in Braga in the fifth round of the Nations League, its first match since Cristiano Ronaldo retired from the national team. The No. 7 shirt that the forward wore for so many years will not be left unused, as the team has already decided who will put it on.



The player is Carlos Forbs, who appears with the No. 7 in the official match sheet published by UEFA. The 22-year-old winger, who plays for Club Brugge, will inherit the number from Ronaldo, even though he has yet to feature in this edition of the Nations League.



The decision has a practical explanation. National teams must assign numbers from 1 to 23 to their squads in this competition, so someone had to take the No. 7. Rafael Leao, who would be the natural candidate, is out injured for both of Portugal’s matches in this window.



For that reason, the assignment is expected to be temporary. Forbs has worn the shirt before, but Leao is the one expected to inherit it permanently once he returns. Before kickoff, though, the number will belong to everyone, as the entire squad is set to walk onto the pitch wearing the No. 7 in a tribute to Ronaldo.



Portugal’s official squad list vs Denmark. (uefa.com)



Who has worn Portugal’s No. 7 before and after Ronaldo?



Before Ronaldo, the shirt belonged to Luis Figo, who wore it at the 1996, 2000, and 2004 European Championships and at the 2002 and 2006 World Cups. Outside of Figo and Ronaldo, only three Portuguese players have worn it in a major tournament: Figueiredo at the 1966 World Cup, Carlos Manuel at Euro 1984, and Jaime Pacheco at the 1986 World Cup.


        


After the 2006 World Cup, Ronaldo took it over, and it stayed with him for the rest of his career, two decades in all. He wore it at five World Cups, from 2010 to 2026, five European Championships, from 2008 to 2024, and the 2019 and 2025 Nations League finals. It only changed hands in the rare matches he missed, which is when other players got to wear it.



Gonçalo Guedes did so in friendlies against Mexico and the United States earlier this year, Forbs wore it in the 9-1 win over Armenia in 2025, and Leao used it in the matches against Denmark and Norway last month, when Ronaldo left the national team’s camp.



Ronaldo’s retirement closes a chapter that lasted almost two decades, and the No. 7 now begins a new one. Forbs will carry it in Braga as a temporary solution, with Leao expected to take over later, but the real question for Portugal is who will be able to wear a shirt that rarely belonged to anyone else, and that carries the weight of two of the greatest names the national team has ever had.

items.title: Guatemala vs Canada: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Guatemala vs Canada in the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League. Guatemala host Canada in a Concacaf Nations League meeting that pits a home side on a short unbeaten run against a visiting squad built around several Premier League and European regulars.
Guatemala come into this one having won 1-0 over Suriname on October 6, following a scoreless draw with the same opponent on October 2. That stretch of back-to-back clean sheets against Suriname shows a team settling defensively under Luis Fernando Tena. A positive result here would keep Guatemala’s momentum going in a competition that carries real weight for their regional standing.
Canada arrive without a recent form line to lean on, but the occasion itself carries its own significance. A Nations League trip to Guatemala is the kind of fixture that tests squad depth away from home conditions. For Jesse Marsch’s group, this match is about banking points and building continuity ahead of the matches still to come in the competition.
Guatemala confirmed lineup
Tena sets Guatemala up in a 4-2-3-1 with Nicholas Hagen behind a back line of Aarón Herrera, José Morales, José Rosales and Allen Yanes. Nicolás Samayoa and Óscar Santis sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking trio of Rubio Rubín, Darwin Lom and Jesús López just behind lone striker Rudy Muñoz. There are no absences to account for, so Tena has his full group available and can lean on the same structure that produced consecutive clean matches against Suriname.
Guatemala confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Nicholas Hagen, Aarón Herrera, José Morales, José Rosales, Allen Yanes, Nicolás Samayoa, Óscar Santis, Rubio Rubín, Darwin Lom, Jesús López, Rudy Muñoz. Coach: Luis Fernando Tena.
Canada confirmed lineup
Marsch lines Canada up in a 4-4-2, with Maxime Crépeau in goal behind a back four of Richie Laryea, Alphonso Davies, Luc De Fougerolles and Joel Waterman. Mathieu Choinière, Tajon Buchanan, Niko Sigur and Liam Millar make up the midfield four, with Jonathan David paired alongside Tani Oluwaseyi up front. With no absences listed, Marsch sends out a full-strength XI that leans on Davies and Buchanan’s width and the partnership of David and Oluwaseyi to carry the attacking load.
Canada confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Maxime Crépeau, Richie Laryea, Alphonso Davies, Mathieu Choinière, Luc De Fougerolles, Joel Waterman, Tajon Buchanan, Niko Sigur, Tani Oluwaseyi, Jonathan David, Liam Millar. Coach: Jesse Marsch.

items.title: Portugal prepares tribute for Cristiano Ronaldo in Nations League, but his presence remains uncertain
items.description:
Portugal’s players will all wear the No. 7 in Braga, and the stadium will stop in the seventh minute to salute Cristiano Ronaldo, though his own attendance remains unclear. 
Portugal will say a symbolic goodbye to Cristiano Ronaldo on Saturday, when it hosts Denmark in the Nations League at the Estadio Municipal de Braga. It will be the team’s first match since the forward announced his retirement from the national team on Nov. 5, although it is still unclear whether he will be in the stands to see it.



The idea took shape in a meeting on Thursday between federation president Pedro Proenca, coach Jorge Jesus, and the team’s three captains: Bernardo Silva, Ruben Dias, and Bruno Fernandes. 



They reportedly agreed that every player will walk onto the pitch wearing the No. 7, the number that Ronaldo made his own during 23 years with the national team. The tribute is also expected to continue during the game, which will be stopped in the seventh minute so that the stadium can give Ronaldo a standing ovation, reportedly with UEFA’s approval.



Off the pitch, the federation has also left Ronaldo’s room at the Cidade do Futebol, the team’s training base, empty during this camp. Even so, there has been no confirmation about whether the Al Nassr striker will attend the stadium, and the reports about the ceremony do not mention any official word on his participation.




Uma história que fica para sempre. 𝙊𝙗𝙧𝙞𝙜𝙖𝙙𝙤 𝙥𝙤𝙧 𝙩𝙪𝙙𝙤, 𝘾𝙖𝙥𝙞𝙩𝙖̃𝙤 🐐⭐️ pic.twitter.com/OSKr7L7xMW— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 5, 2026




Jorge Jesus reacts to the tribute



The Portugal coach was asked about the homage at his press conference on the eve of the match, where he explained that the idea did not originate with him or his staff. “Such decisions are always the responsibility of the Portuguese Football Federation, more specifically its football and sporting departments and its president,” he said.


        


Even so, he was quick to praise it: “It is brilliant because nobody can forget the 23 years Cris spent with the national team, what he achieved for Portugal, and the impact he has had on the world of football”.



Jesus, who worked with Ronaldo for a year, added that he knows him well and understands how important he is “not only to the younger players and the next generation, but to everyone”. He closed with a reminder of what the player means for the country: “We must never forget that he is a legend of Portuguese football”.



The tribute in Braga gives Portugal a chance to say goodbye properly to a player whose exit from the national team did not come in the best way, after weeks of tension with Jesus. For Ronaldo, who spent 23 years with the team, it could be the closing chapter that the circumstances of his retirement did not allow, if he decides to be there.

items.title: Why is Virgil van Dijk not playing for the Netherlands vs Greece in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 5?
items.description:
Virgil van Dijk is out for the Netherlands against Greece due to injury, so Xavi gave the armband to Frenkie de Jong in the Nations League clash. 
Virgil van Dijk will not be available for the Netherlands in their Nations League clash against Greece on Friday in Amsterdam. The Liverpool captain withdrew from Xavi’s squad due to a fitness issue, which also rules him out of the team’s final group match against Germany on Monday in Berlin.



The Dutch football association (KNVB) confirmed the news in a statement on Monday. “Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey aren’t fit enough to feature in the upcoming Nations League matches. No replacements will be called up,” it said. The decision leaves Xavi with a 23-player squad for the two games, and it also takes the Sunderland striker out of the picture.



The withdrawal came a day after Van Dijk played the full 90 minutes in Liverpool’s 3-1 win at Crystal Palace, a match in which he kept up his record of playing every minute in the Premier League this season.



The KNVB said he did not return fit from that game, although the nature of the problem has not been disclosed. According to The Athletic’s James Pearce, the defender had been dealing with a minor injury issue in recent weeks, so skipping the international break appears to be a precaution to avoid aggravating it.




Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey aren’t fit enough to feature in the upcoming Nations League matches. ❌No replacements will be called up. pic.twitter.com/TB5aTNUcn3— OnsOranje (@OnsOranje) November 9, 2026




The absence also interrupts a milestone run for the Dutch captain, who reached his 100th cap in the 2-1 win over Serbia in early October. For the Netherlands, who are battling Greece and Germany for a top-two finish in Group A, it means going into these two decisive matches without their leader at the back.



Who replaces Van Dijk in the Netherlands’ lineup?


        


Xavi responded to the absence of his captain by building a back four with Denzel Dumfries, Jan Paul van Hecke, Micky van de Ven, and Jurrien Timber, with Bart Verbruggen in goal. Van Hecke and Van de Ven form the central pairing, which leaves the Brighton defender with the task of filling the spot Van Dijk usually occupies.



The captain’s armband, in turn, goes to Frenkie de Jong, who anchors a midfield trio completed by Jerdy Veerman and Tijjani Reijnders. Further forward, Xavi opted for Crysencio Summerville, Donyell Malen, and Cody Gakpo as his front three.



The decision also marks De Jong’s comeback with the national team. The Barcelona midfielder had not played for the Netherlands since the 2026 World Cup, where he suffered a knee injury, and only returned to club action in late October.

items.title: Lionel Scaloni’s renewal puts him on course to break a historic record as Argentina coach
items.description:
Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030 opens the door for him to surpass legends like Menotti and Bilardo and write his name in Argentina’s history books. 
Lionel Scaloni’s renewal does not only secure Argentina’s coach for the next cycle, it also opens the door to making history from the bench. The Argentine Football Association (AFA) confirmed on Thursday, through its president Claudio Tapia, that the coach will continue through 2030, and has put him on course for a mark that no Argentine coach has achieved before.



If Scaloni remains in charge until the 2030 World Cup, he will become the first coach to lead Argentina at three World Cups: Qatar 2022, the 2026 edition in North America, and the Centenary World Cup in 2030.



In doing so, he would surpass the marks of César Luis Menotti, who coached the team in 1978 and 1982, and Carlos Bilardo, who did so in 1986 and 1990, both with two tournaments each.



The record comes after a 2026 World Cup that ended in heartbreak, with Argentina losing the final against Spain on July 19, a result that left his continuity in doubt. “The blow of not having won the final was hard, and the first thing that comes to your mind is to think about what to do, see what comes and try to recharge your batteries,” Scaloni explained at the final press conference.




Lionel Scaloni, chasing more moments like this. 🥹🇦🇷 #FIFAWorldCup pic.twitter.com/xbCvokDiDr— FIFA World Cup (@FIFAWorldCup) November 12, 2026




Almost four months after the final at MetLife Stadium, Scaloni has finally decided to accept the offer to stay on as coach and will look to keep making history with Argentina.



Scaloni’s résumé: the records he holds and the ones he chases


        


Few coaches have built a case as strong as Scaloni’s. In 107 matches in charge of Argentina, he has recorded 79 wins, 18 draws, and 10 losses, and he has won four official titles: the 2021 Copa America, the 2022 Finalissima, the 2022 World Cup, and the 2024 Copa America. That puts him in second place among Argentina’s most successful coaches by trophies, tied with Alfio Basile and behind Guillermo Stabile, who won seven.



Some of those marks already belong to him. Scaloni is the coach who has directed the most World Cup matches (13) and won the most (10) in Argentina’s history and he also led the team through a 36-game unbeaten streak between 2019 and 2022, which surpassed the previous record of 31 held by Basile’s team. The run only ended in the opening match of the Qatar World Cup, a 2-1 loss to Saudi Arabia.



Stabile’s numbers, however, remain within reach. Scaloni needs five more wins to become the coach with the most victories in the history of the national team and he needs 18 more matches to surpass the 124 that Stabile directed, something he could achieve as early as the 2028 Copa America.



With his contract now running through 2030, Scaloni has the time and the tournaments to turn those pursuits into reality. To match Stabile’s seven titles, he would need to win the 2028 Copa America and the 2030 World Cup, and also the Finalissima against Spain, a title that for now remains pending.

items.title: Lionel Scaloni reveals decision on Lionel Messi’s No. 10 after renewing with Argentina
items.description:
One of the first questions of Argentina’s new era is who will inherit the No. 10 shirt left vacant by Lionel Messi. After the Argentine Football Association confirmed Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030, the coach addressed the subject at a press conference in Buenos Aires, ahead of Friday’s friendly against Uruguay at La Bombonera. Scaloni […] 
One of the first questions of Argentina’s new era is who will inherit the No. 10 shirt left vacant by Lionel Messi. After the Argentine Football Association confirmed Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030, the coach addressed the subject at a press conference in Buenos Aires, ahead of Friday’s friendly against Uruguay at La Bombonera.



Scaloni made it clear that, for now, the shirt will not have a new owner. “In this match we won’t give it to anyone. We haven’t thought about who we’ll give it to when it becomes obligatory,” he said, meaning that, at least for this FIFA window, nobody will wear the No. 10.



He did explain, however, what he would like to happen when that moment arrives. “We hope that the day we do it, it’s forever, and that we don’t keep changing it. The idea is to give it to the player who can keep it,” Scaloni said, which suggests that the number will be reserved for a player who can wear it for years, as Messi did.



The obligation comes from FIFA, which requires national teams in official competitions to number their squads consecutively from 1 to 23, so the No. 10 cannot simply be skipped and must be assigned to a specific player. That means Scaloni will eventually have to decide who wears it, although for now he insists the matter is not something that worries him.




#SelecciónMayor La historia continúa… pic.twitter.com/Wv4oCKpCuU— 🇦🇷 Selección Argentina ⭐⭐⭐ (@Argentina) November 12, 2026




Scaloni on life without Messi: ‘I hope he’s happy’



Even without Messi in the squad, his name was present throughout Scaloni’s press conference. When the coach was asked how Argentina will play without him, he was clear about what it means for the team’s identity. “There’s no way to try to play without him; now we’ll try to play a similar game but with different alternatives,” Scaloni said, acknowledging that the style will not change, but the players who carry it out will.


        


He also admitted that he has not yet discussed his renewal with his former captain. “I haven’t spoken with Leo, I hope he’s happy that we can continue,” Scaloni said, a comment that shows how much of the project still revolves around Messi’s approval.



For the coach, however, the next step is to build on what is already in place. “It’s an advantage that we have players who already know us, but this is football and what matters is that those who come adapt as soon as possible to what we want, which is what this is about: getting to know each other and training together,” he explained.



With the No. 10 shirt still without an owner and Messi’s reaction to his renewal still unknown, Scaloni begins his new cycle on Friday against Uruguay at La Bombonera. The match will be the first real chance to see how Argentina’s style holds up, with younger players and without the player who defined the last era.

Argentina confirm Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030 as new era begins without Lionel Messi
items.description:
Argentina confirmed Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030, with a new era starting without Lionel Messi and a change in the coach’s team. 
Argentina has secured its coach for the next cycle just as it begins a new chapter without Lionel Messi. The Argentine Football Association (AFA) confirmed on Thursday that Lionel Scaloni will continue at the helm of the national team through 2030.



The announcement was made by AFA president Claudio Tapia during a press conference in Ezeiza, alongside the coach himself. “It’s a very special day for the Argentine national team and Argentine soccer. We’re going to officially announce the renewal of Lionel Scaloni for the period 2027 to 2030,” Tapia told reporters.



The coach said his motivation is the same as when he took charge in 2018. “We have the same hope and desire as the first day, otherwise it would be impossible to be here,” Scaloni explained. He also said that this will be a new era after Messi’s departure, in which new players will emerge. “A new era begins, we will give a chance to kids who are pushing from behind,” he added.



The extension is a reward for a cycle that has brought four official titles since his arrival: the 2021 Copa America, the 2022 Finalissima, the 2022 World Cup, and the 2024 Copa America.




𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐢𝐬 𝐒𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐧𝐢 𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐥 𝟐𝟎𝟑𝟎 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/3W3O5xEvI5— Selección Argentina in English (@AFASeleccionEN) November 12, 2026




Across 107 matches, Scaloni has recorded 79 wins, 18 draws, and 10 losses, and his first test of this new stage will come right away, in the friendlies against Uruguay on Friday at La Bombonera and Costa Rica next Tuesday in Cordoba.



Walter Samuel leaves Scaloni’s coaching staff


        


The renewal comes with one change in the coach’s team, as Walter Samuel will leave the national team’s staff after eight years by Scaloni’s side. The coach himself made it official at the press conference: “Walter Samuel, as I had already advanced, will start his career alone. Eternal gratitude to a friend, I wish him the best because he was an important part of our staff and it’s fair that he can begin his path”.



Samuel will still be on the bench for both of those matches, which will be his last. The former Real Madrid defender had been part of the staff since the beginning of the cycle in 2018, alongside Pablo Aimar, and his specific role was set pieces and the defensive side of the team.



The coach also made clear that, for now, there will be no replacement for Samuel. “In principle we won’t add anyone. We believe we can continue like this and that’s what we’re going to try. We stay as we are,” Scaloni said, although he did not rule out changes later on: “In any case, we have people in youth who could give us a hand, and that would be in the future”.



With Samuel’s departure and a new generation knocking at the door, Scaloni begins this new cycle with the same group of collaborators but a very different roster. Argentina’s next challenge will be to show that the project can keep winning without Messi, starting with the Uruguay friendly on Friday.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement adds emotional twist to son’s Portugal U-17 debut as teenager comes close to dream first goal
items.description:
While the legendary forward has brought his international career to an end, his 16-year-old son has taken another important step towards following in his footsteps, attracting attention during a memorable appearance for the youth national team. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and his eldest son, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr., have reached two very different milestones in Portugal’s soccer history within the space of a week. While the legendary forward has brought his international career to an end, his 16-year-old son has taken another important step towards following in his footsteps, attracting attention during a memorable appearance for the youth national team.



Ronaldo Jr. made his Portugal Under-17 debut on Thursday, featuring in a European Championship qualifying match against Andorra. The occasion carried additional significance because of who was watching from the stands and the timing of his father’s recent announcement.



The young Selecao secured a comfortable 4-0 victory over Andorra at Cidade do Futebol in Oeiras, making a positive start to its Under-17 European Championship qualifying campaign. Diego Farinha scored twice, while Kaua Miranda converted a penalty and Rafael Cabral added another goal in the second half.



Ronaldo Jr. entered the match as a substitute in the 73rd minute, replacing Victor Bastianele with the result already effectively decided. Wearing the number 18 shirt, the Al-Nassr academy forward had limited time to make an impression but still came close to marking his debut with a goal.



Moments Cristiano Jr got subbed on.Portugal U17 are 4–0 up against Andorra.🇵🇹🇦🇩 pic.twitter.com/YgRDbvy3Ck— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) November 12, 2026 



The teenager comes close to memorable first goal



The biggest opportunity arrived late in the match when Ronaldo Jr. connected with a cross from the left inside the penalty area. His header narrowly missed the target, denying him a dream start at Under-17 level and leaving Portugal’s scoreline unchanged.



The teenager’s physical presence was already noticeable, although he still has plenty of time to develop as a player. His latest appearance represents another stage in an international journey that has already included spells with Portugal’s Under-15 and Under-16 teams.



¡CÓMO NO RECORDARTE! 🥹Cristiano Jr. debutó con la Selección Sub-17 de Portugal y nos hizo acordarnos del Bicho 🐐🇵🇹(Vía X: mousaqi/Sporting) pic.twitter.com/ojYfUv0UET— ESPN.com.mx (@ESPNmx) November 12, 2026 



Portugal’s senior stars watch Ronaldo’s son make his debut



The occasion became even more emotional because members of the Selecao’s senior national team were reportedly present to watch the youth side in action. Players including Vitinha, Joao Cancelo, Joao Felix and Joao Neves were among those following the match at the national training center.



Their presence created a memorable connection between Portugal’s established stars and the next generation. However, one particularly important figure was missing from the occasion: Ronaldo himself, who had announced his international retirement only a week earlier.



The Portuguese National Team players watching the U17 game.Cristiano Ronaldo would have been present to watch his son play, if he hadn't retired.🥲 pic.twitter.com/jZ2s0OdIiq— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) November 12, 2026 



The timing prompted an emotional reaction from soccer fans, with social media users highlighting what the moment might have looked like had the veteran forward remained available for Portugal.



What comes next for Ronaldo Jr. and Portugal U-17?



Portugal’s qualifying campaign continues with upcoming matches against Bulgaria and Serbia, scheduled for November 14 and November 17, respectively. Those fixtures will give Ronaldo Jr. further opportunities to earn minutes and establish himself at this level.



His debut against Andorra may have lasted only around 17 minutes, but it represented an important personal milestone. With his father stepping away from international soccer, the teenager now has the opportunity to create his own story in the same national colors, with the support of some of Portugal’s biggest stars.

items.title: Czechia vs Spain: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Czechia vs Spain in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League. Czechia and Spain meet again just days after their last meeting, and this time the venue flips with Czechia hosting in this Nations League fixture.
Czechia have lost all three of their recent matches, falling 0-3 to England on October 6, 1-3 to Spain on October 3, and 0-2 to England on September 29. The run has left them without a win across this stretch, and a result against Spain would offer a rare lift after back-to-back shutout defeats to England sandwiched around the first meeting with this same opponent. For Czechia, the game is really about stopping the bleeding before the next camp.
Spain, by contrast, arrive on the back of three straight wins, beating Croatia 2-1 on October 6, Czechia 3-1 on October 3, and Croatia 4-1 on September 29. That stretch has them scoring freely and conceding little, with nine goals put away across the three games. A repeat result here would extend the momentum and confirm Spain as the form side of this Nations League group.
Czechia confirmed lineup
Czechia are set up in a 4-2-3-1, with Antonín Kinský behind a back line of Vladimír Coufal, Štěpán Chaloupek, Ladislav Krejčí and Jiří Sláma. Tomáš Souček and Alex Král look to anchor midfield, giving the side some physical presence in front of the defense, while Kryštof Daněk, Lukáš Ambros and Lukáš Červ support Adam Hložek as the central striker. There are no listed absences, so this looks like close to a full-strength selection, but the group still has to find a way to defend better after conceding five goals in two matches against England and three more against Spain earlier this month.
Czechia confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Matěj Kovář, Vladimír Coufal, David Jurásek, Alex Král, David Zima, Ladislav Krejčí, Lukáš Ambros, Lukáš Červ, Ryan Naderi, Adam Hložek, Lukáš Provod. Coach: Santi Denia.
Spain confirmed lineup
Spain line up in the same 4-2-3-1 shape, with Unai Simón in goal behind Pedro Porro, Pau Cubarsí, Dean Huijsen and Alex Grimaldo. Fabián Ruiz and Martín Zubimendi sit in the double pivot, and Fermín López joins Jorge De Frutos and Álex Baena behind Ferran Torres in attack. Coach Luis De La Fuente has no reported absences to work around, and the continuity in personnel reflects a team that has scored at least two goals in each of its last three outings.
Spain confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Unai Simón, Pedro Porro, Marc Cucurella, Fabián Ruiz, Pau Cubarsí, Dean Huijsen, Yéremy Pino, Martín Zubimendi, Ferran Torres, Fermín López, Álex Baena. Coach: Luis de la Fuente.

items.title: Why is Bukayo Saka not playing for England vs Croatia in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 5?
items.description:
England will face Croatia at Wembley without one of their most important attackers. Bukayo Saka, the Arsenal winger who has been Thomas Tuchel’s first choice on the right flank, is still recovering from a quad injury and will not be available for Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, nor for the rest of […] 
England will face Croatia at Wembley without one of their most important attackers. Bukayo Saka, the Arsenal winger who has been Thomas Tuchel’s first choice on the right flank, is still recovering from a quad injury and will not be available for Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, nor for the rest of the international break.



Saka suffered the injury after just 10 minutes of Arsenal’s Champions League match against Bayern Munich last month, and he has since missed Arsenal’s last five games.



There were initial fears that he could be out for up to eight weeks, but Mikel Arteta has been cautiously optimistic about his recovery. “The way it happened, it wasn’t a really aggressive action,” the Arsenal manager said ahead of the win over Hull on Nov. 7.



“So that gives you some hope as well that the tissue will repair in a more efficient and faster way as well and he has some very good symptoms right now. So we have to wait and see,” the Spanish coach concluded about Saka’s recovery, as the winger still has no confirmed return date.



"Unfortunately he's going to be out for a while"Mikel Arteta provides an injury update on Bukayo Saka 🏥 pic.twitter.com/pOyzd8csM8— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 6, 2026 



The absence comes at a decisive moment for England, who have won three of their four Nations League games without conceding a goal, and whose only loss was a 3-2 defeat at Wembley against Spain in late September.



A draw against Croatia would be enough to guarantee a place in the quarterfinals, while top spot in the group will be decided on Sunday in Madrid, where Tuchel’s side will face Spain without Saka again.


        


Who will replace Saka on England’s right wing?



Tuchel has already identified who will try to fill the gap left by Saka. “I think it’s Morgan Rogers for us and then it will be Rio [Ngumoha] on that side. He played there for Liverpool and impressed in the last camp,” the England coach said, naming the Chelsea forward as the likeliest to start on the right against Croatia, with Ngumoha as the alternative.



He also mentioned other possibilities: “Josh King can maybe play there, we will try this, and then Morgan Gibbs-White can play on the wing. We need runners there who can attack through the lines, so I think we have options”.



The options are also reduced because Noni Madueke, who deputized for Saka at the World Cup in the summer, was left out of the squad. Tuchel admitted that the decision was not easy: “It’s a close call and difficult decision not to bring Noni, but we stick with the group that we had and give them our trust”.



Whoever gets the nod on Thursday will face a double challenge, because Saka will also be absent on Sunday against Spain, a match that could decide who finishes first in the group. For Tuchel, the performance of his replacement against Croatia could therefore be an indication of how England will approach the next game without one of their key attackers.

items.title: Why is Lamine Yamal not playing for Spain vs Czechia in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 5?
items.description:
Luis de la Fuente’s side will travel to Prague looking to maintain its impressive run and strengthen its position at the top of Group A3, although the Barcelona youngster will be missing from the squad for a reason that has attracted considerable attention. 
Lamine Yamal’s absence is set to be one of the biggest talking points when Spain faces Czechia in its 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 5 clash. Luis de la Fuente’s side will travel to Prague looking to maintain its impressive run and strengthen its position at the top of Group A3, although the Barcelona youngster will be missing from the squad for a reason that has attracted considerable attention.



Spain has dominated Group A3, winning all four of its opening matches to secure qualification for the quarter-finals. The reigning world champion has collected 12 points, scoring 12 goals along the way, and currently sits three points ahead of England.



De la Fuente’s side began the campaign with a memorable 3-2 victory over England before beating Croatia 4-1 and Czechia 3-1. La Roja then completed another win over Croatia, 2-1, and will now aim to extend its impressive winning streak before facing England in its final group match.



Spain has also enjoyed an excellent run across all competitions, winning its last 11 matches. Its opponent, meanwhile, has struggled throughout the campaign and has yet to collect a single point.



Victor Munoz of Spain shoots and misses vs Czechia



Czechia face uphill battle against the world champion



Czechia has lost all four of its Nations League fixtures, leaving it bottom of Group A3 and facing the possibility of relegation to League B. Its defeats include losses to Croatia and England at home, followed by a 3-1 defeat against Spain and a 3-0 setback at Wembley.



The national team has also lost five consecutive matches across all competitions, with its last victory coming in a friendly against Guatemala in June. Although Czechia can still finish third, stopping Spain will be a difficult task given the visitors’ current form and their dominant record in this fixture.



PositionTeamPlayedW-D-LPoints1.Spain44-0-0122.England43-0-193.Croatia41-0-334.Czechia40-0-40UEFA Nations League A – Group 3 Standings



Spain has won six of its eight previous meetings with Czechia, while the other two ended in draws. Czechia has never beaten La Roja, adding another challenge for Santi Denia’s team ahead of Thursday’s encounter.



Why Lamine Yamal is missing against Czechia



The reason behind Yamal’s absence is an injury sustained while playing for Barcelona against Atletico Madrid over the weekend. The 19-year-old is nursing a knee problem, which has ruled him out of Spain’s trip to Prague.



According to the reports surrounding the squad announcement, Yamal is expected to join the national team after the Czech Republic fixture and prepare for Sunday’s meeting with England. His absence also allows De la Fuente to manage the workload of one of his most important attacking players.



Lamine Yamal of Spain.



The Spanish teenager has been heavily involved for both the Blaugrana and Spain this season, making his availability an important consideration ahead of the upcoming international fixtures. The decision to leave him out against Czechia also allows the coaching staff to avoid taking unnecessary risks with his fitness.



Yamal is not the only notable absentee for Spain, with Rodri ruled out because of a minor injury, and Mikel Oyarzabal also unavailable because of illness. The forward is another important attacking option for De la Fuente, although his potential return for the England match remains uncertain.
